wu: Play 'Mime the Animal': Teacher mimes a wild animal, students guess 'Is it a lion?' or 'Is it an elephant?' using target vocabulary. Students take turns miming.
wuAlt: Play 'Animal Charades': Students draw an animal flashcard and act it out for the class to guess.
Play 'Flashcard Race': Two teams race to slap the correct animal flashcard when the teacher says the name.
pres: Show flashcards of lion, elephant, monkey, snake. Model sentences: 'A lion is big. It has got a mane. It lives in Africa.' Drill pronunciation. Check understanding by asking 'What has a mane?' and 'Where does a snake live?'
presAlt: Tell a short story about a trip to the zoo using the target animals and facts.
Use a video clip of animals and pause to elicit facts from students.
prac: Play 'Guess the Animal': Teacher describes an animal ('It is big and grey. It has a trunk.'), students guess the animal. Students then describe animals in pairs using 'It is... It has got... It lives...'
pracAlt: Complete a 'My Animal Fact' worksheet by filling in blanks with size, body part, and location.
Play 'Animal Bingo' with fact clues instead of names.
ls: Listen to a short audio recording of a child presenting their animal facts. Students listen and fill in a simple chart with the animal name and one fact they heard.
re: Play 'Months Line-Up': Students get a month card and line up in order from January to December. Teacher asks 'What month comes after March?' to review the year.
prod: Survey and Graph Activity: Students ask 3 classmates 'What is your favorite wild animal?' and tally results. As a group, they draw a simple bar graph on the board to show the most popular animal.
rw: Create 'My Wish for 2027' Craft: Students write one sentence 'I wish...' on a star-shaped paper (e.g., 'I wish I can see a lion.') and decorate it. They stick it on a class New Year poster.
st: Sing 'Happy New Year' song with actions. Read a short picture story about animals celebrating the New Year. End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students match animal flashcards to fact cards, reading the facts aloud.
One student thinks of an animal, others ask 'Is it big? Can it fly?' to guess.
Students ask classmates about favorite animals and draw a bar graph.
Students write a wish for 2027 on a star and decorate it.
Students line up in order from January to December.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a second, more complex fact about their animal using 'It can...'
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame 'It is... It has got...' to write their facts.
hw: Prepare 2 facts about a wild animal to tell the class next week.
Write your wish on the class poster template.
Draw a picture of your favorite wild animal and label it.
tip: Use the animal theme to connect with local Moroccan wildlife like the Barbary macaque or desert fox to make the lesson more relatable and culturally relevant.
